prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1029; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- Witnesses and the officer say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Reported today by the claimant, who is not represented by an attorney, following a rear-end collision at a city intersection. The claimant reports neck and back discomfort and says they were the driver of the stopped vehicle that was struck from behind.

Entry 2: Spoke with the other driver, who confirms the collision happened as the claimant described and says they were following too closely in slow traffic. Took the other driver's insurance details and their statement.

Entry 3: Photos from the scene and the damage on both vehicles line up with the impact described by the claimant. Rear bumper and trunk damage on the claimant's car is consistent with a rear-end impact at low speed.

Entry 4: Requested the police report. The responding officer's notes say the claimant was not inside the vehicle when the collision occurred, which differs from the account given to me so far. Will clarify this with the claimant.

Entry 5: Called the claimant to ask about the discrepancy in the police notes. The claimant gave the same account of the collision as in the first report and said the earlier note was likely mistaken, adding that they got out only after the other car stopped.

Entry 6: Two independent witnesses gave statements that match the other driver's version of the impact. Neither witness could confirm where the claimant was seated at the moment of contact, so the question remains open.

Entry 7: Checked the claimant's vehicle history. No prior damage to the rear of the car is recorded, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy's effective coverage period. The driver is named on the policy.

Entry 8: The claimant has been seen by a treating provider for a back strain. The injury is plausible for a collision of this type, and the claimant reports no earlier injury to the same area. Treatment has run somewhat longer than is typical for this diagnosis, so I've asked for the treatment notes.

Entry 9: Received the treatment notes and reviewed the medical timeline. Records show consistent complaints from the first visit onward, and the claimant has described the symptoms the same way in every conversation. No prior records for the same body region were found.

Entry 10: Reviewed the full file with the supervisor. The impact, vehicle damage and the other driver's account all support the reported collision. The open item is the officer's note on the claimant's position in the vehicle, which needs to be resolved before a settlement offer is made.
